solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Foresee resistance after Putin's first order

indicators.note: after places the resistance letter behind Putin's first letter
first asks for the opening letter of the word Putin's

parts.note: R is the physics symbol for electrical resistance
an edict is an official order or decree

explanation.surface: A forecast that a Russian leader's first command will meet resistance.
explanation.definitionFit: To foresee something is to forecast it before it happens, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Dill regularly stocked by fruit seller

indicators.note: stocked by means the picked letters are held within the fruit

parts.note: a pear is a fruit

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of Dill

explanation.surface: A greengrocer sells dill alongside the fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedlar is a travelling seller of small goods.

clue.text: Character I'd cut out being

indicators.note: cut out means the letters of I'd are removed from the character word

parts.note: a person's identity is their character
I'd gives the letters I and D

explanation.surface: A personality is edited out of existence.
explanation.definitionFit: An entity is a thing with distinct existence, a being.

clue.text: Uncertain to order dinner if tie not right

indicators.note: to order means the letters are rearranged
not says the right letter is missing from the rearranged pool

explanation.surface: Unsure whether to order a meal if not wearing the right tie.
explanation.walkthrough: DINNER IF TIE has one R more than the answer: 'not right' removes it, and 'to order' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Indefinite means not clearly fixed or determined, hence uncertain.

clue.text: Subject to choice? Not quite

indicators.note: not quite means the choice word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: a pick is a choice, as in take your pick

explanation.surface: A matter that's up for choice, but not entirely.
explanation.definitionFit: A topic is a subject for discussion.

clue.text: The Entertainer, for example, almost perfectly jolly

parts.note: The Entertainer is a stage play by John Osborne

indicators.note: almost means the word for perfectly loses its final letter

parts.note: full can mean perfectly or completely, as in knowing full well

explanation.surface: A music-hall entertainer is described as being in near-perfect good humour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims FULL to FUL. The Entertainer is John Osborne's 1957 play about a fading music-hall comic, so it is a play rather than a performer.
explanation.definitionFit: Jolly and playful are near synonyms, both describing a light-hearted, fun-loving mood.

clue.text: Awful temper with nan going on and on

indicators.note: awful signals the letters of temper and nan are badly jumbled

explanation.surface: Grandma's terrible mood seems to last forever.
explanation.definitionFit: Permanent means lasting indefinitely, continuing without end.

clue.text: Skilled Liberal Democrat losing his head

indicators.note: losing his head means the politician's name drops its first letter

parts.note: Vince Cable is a former Liberal Democrat leader

explanation.surface: A competent Lib Dem politician is decapitated.
explanation.walkthrough: Vince Cable led the Liberal Democrats, a UK political party, from 2017 to 2019.
explanation.definitionFit: Able means capable or competent, so skilled fits.

clue.text: Visit common

definitions.meaning: to go to a place often
happening often, as in a regular occurrence

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to visit habitually; the adjective means occurring often, so common.

clue.text: Starts to see the eels in large ship — one's likely to catch a lot

definitions.text: one's likely to catch a lot

indicators.note: in places those initials inside the ship

parts.note: a liner is a large passenger ship

indicators.note: starts to takes the first letters of see, the and eels

explanation.surface: Passengers on an ocean liner watch eels being caught.
explanation.walkthrough: The fishing picture misleads: the one who catches a lot catches words, not fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A listener catches what is said, hearing a great deal; a playful cryptic definition.

clue.text: Old girlfriend given diamonds

parts.note: a date is someone you are romantically seeing
D is the card-suit abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: An elderly girlfriend is presented with diamond jewellery.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dated is old-fashioned or out of date, so old is a fair synonym.

clue.text: Matches — each golfer is after a decent score

indicators.note: after puts the each-and-golfer pieces behind the decent score

parts.note: par is a good, standard score on a golf hole
all means each in sport scores, as in two all
Ernie Els is a South African golfer

explanation.surface: Every golfer is aiming to make par on the hole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'each' gives ALL as in a tied score like 'three all'.
explanation.definitionFit: Parallels are things that correspond to one another, and matches as a noun means equivalents.

clue.text: Forced frail cat I upset to eat one

indicators.note: to eat means the shuffled letters take in another piece
upset means the letters of frail cat I are knocked into a new order

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A fragile cat gets upset about being made to eat something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns FRAILCATI into ARTIFCIAL, and 'to eat' puts I (one) inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A forced smile is an artificial one, not natural or genuine.

clue.text: Stable bank, by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it says a word for bank is said aloud

parts.note: a shore is the bank of a sea or lake

explanation.surface: A financial institution is described as sound, judging by its reputation.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech SHORE and SURE can sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Sure footing is stable footing; both mean firm and secure.

clue.text: Dine out, breaking diet if discovered

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of Dine are disordered
breaking means the letters of diet if are broken up and mixed in

explanation.surface: Eating out, breaking a diet, if found out.
explanation.definitionFit: Identified means recognised or found out, so discovered is a synonym.

clue.text: Liberty's desire for some Scotch?

definitions.meaning: the Scots, playfully called Scotch, partly want Scotland to leave the UK

explanation.surface: Someone who feels free fancies a drop of whisky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scotch' looks like whisky but means the Scots, many of whom want Scotland separated from the United Kingdom.
explanation.definitionFit: Independence is freedom from outside control, which is what liberty means.

clue.text: Men quite badly fixing Peugeot's first gear

indicators.note: fixing means the shuffled letters hold another piece in place
badly means the letters of men quite are scrambled
first takes the initial letter of Peugeot's

explanation.surface: Mechanics make a poor job of repairing a French car's gearbox.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' turns MENQUITE into EQUIMENT, and 'fixing' sets P (Peugeot's first) inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Equipment is gear in the sense of tools or kit.

clue.text: Small copper disc found on hill — one could carve it into something

definitions.text: one could carve it into something

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
an LP is a long-playing record
a tor is a rocky hill

explanation.surface: A small copper disc turns up on a hillside, perhaps a carved relic.
explanation.definitionFit: A sculptor carves stone or wood into works of art.

clue.text: Violent illegal immigrants? Almost the opposite around outskirts of Auckland

indicators.note: around means the trimmed word goes round the other letters
almost means the opposite word loses its final letter

parts.note: the inverse is the opposite

indicators.note: outskirts of takes the outer letters of Auckland

explanation.surface: Violent illegal migrants are said to be on the outskirts of Auckland.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a whimsical definition: invaders are hardly immigrants, but the setter stretches the idea for the surface's sake.
explanation.definitionFit: Invaders enter a country by force, which the question mark loosely likens to violent illegal immigration.

clue.text: Building prisoner's training in to get released

parts.note: a con is a convict, a prisoner

indicators.note: to get released means the word in is let out of the training word

parts.note: instructing someone is training them

explanation.surface: A convict's work-skills course aims to help him earn his release.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get released' removes IN from INSTRUCTING, leaving STRUCTING; the 's of prisoner's is no letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Constructing a house means building it, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Who might appear in Treasure Island from page 26

definitions.text: Who might appear in Treasure Island

parts.note: the answer to 26 across, meaning annoyed

explanation.surface: A character who might turn up in Stevenson's adventure novel, starting on page 26.
explanation.definitionFit: Treasure Island is full of buccaneers like Long John Silver, the classic example of a seafaring robber.

clue.text: If not fun, when female's gone there's a smaller amount

indicators.note: gone means the female letter disappears from fun

parts.note: less means a smaller amount

explanation.surface: Without a woman around, there's less fun to be had.
explanation.definitionFit: Unless means except if, that is, if not.

clue.text: Head's idle

definitions.meaning: ..., from rhyming slang ... of bread, means the head
to ... about is to be idle

explanation.walkthrough: Use your loaf means use your head, from Cockney rhyming slang loaf of bread = head.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhyming slang gives head, and to laze about is the verb sense of idling.

clue.text: Work attitude creates hostility

parts.note: op is short for opus, a musical work
a position is a stance or attitude on an issue

explanation.surface: A bad attitude at work stirs up ill feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: Opposition is resistance or antagonism, so hostility is a fair synonym.

clue.text: Band in studio as I speak

indicators.note: in signals that the letters are found inside studio as I speak

explanation.surface: Someone describes a music group in the recording studio right now.
explanation.walkthrough: Oasis is the Manchester rock band of the Gallagher brothers.
explanation.definitionFit: The British rock group led by the Gallagher brothers, an example of a band.

clue.text: Forced to have flipping cheese

indicators.note: flipping means the cheese word is turned back to front

parts.note: Edam is a Dutch cheese

explanation.surface: Someone is forced to eat the blasted cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' looks like a mild British expletive but tells you to turn the word round.
explanation.definitionFit: Made someone do something means compelled or forced them.

clue.text: Youngsters get a sneer when dressed up

indicators.note: dressing up disguises, so the letters of get a sneer appear in a new form

explanation.surface: Young people sneer when made to wear their smart clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Teenagers are young people aged thirteen to nineteen.

clue.text: Annoyed at getting into rage

indicators.note: getting into means the small word at goes inside the word for rage

parts.note: ire is anger or rage

explanation.surface: Someone becomes annoyed when they fly into a rage.
explanation.definitionFit: Irate means angry, so annoyed is a mild synonym.

clue.text: Show a high regard for detail

explanation.definitionFit: The verb sense is to esteem; the noun sense is a particular aspect or point.

clue.text: Students initially notice head's misery

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of Students

parts.note: an ad is an advertisement or notice
a ness is a headland, a head of land

explanation.surface: Students first spot the head teacher's unhappiness.
explanation.walkthrough: NESS (as in Loch Ness or Dungeness) is a headland, a crossword staple for head.
explanation.definitionFit: Misery and sadness both describe deep unhappiness.
